title: US investigates whether Iran is behind cyberattacks and bomb threats against tankers, ynet reports citing WSJ
date_note: The ynet page gives no earlier day; it cites a Wall Street Journal report from overnight Monday to Tuesday (24 November). Attacks cited include September ones.
geo_basis: United States, where the investigation and the Coast Guard response are reported; the ships' locations vary
summary: Israeli outlet ynet, relaying a Wall Street Journal report, says US officials are investigating whether Iran is behind dozens of cyberattacks on oil and gas ships, some with bomb threats to crews. The report says Iran is the main suspect and Russia is also considered possible, while a Trump administration official said there was no evidence yet of Iranian involvement. The operator of VL Prosperity confirmed a US cyber check on board.
plain: Ynet, citing the Wall Street Journal, says US officials are investigating whether Iran is behind dozens of cyberattacks on oil and gas ships. A Trump administration official said there is no evidence yet.
exec: Ynet reports the US is investigating cyberattacks and bomb threats on oil and gas ships, some bound for US ports; Iran is the main suspect, not confirmed.
action: No action needed; for awareness. The report says the US Coast Guard urges shipping companies to report suspicious activity and use its free resources.

validation.note: One publisher read (ynet, Hebrew), relaying a WSJ report that was not read; the US Coast Guard declined to comment on specific attacks.
